segments: First Jubilee.
Patriarchs.
God, and he drove away the wild beasts (or locusts/caterpillars) that were destroying the land of the Chaldeans
and eating their crops.
And at this time Belus died,
and the second king of Assyria, Ninus his son, arose for fifty-two years.
And he built Nineveh.
And after it were built Rehoboth, Resen, and Calneh (Calah?):
that is, Arbela, Resh'ayna, and Seleucia.
And Jerusalem also was built by Melchizedek the Canaanite.
And Abraham burned the temple of idols that was in Ur of the Chaldeans.
And Haran his brother went in to extinguish the fire,
and he was burned there.
And for this reason Abraham, when he was sixty years old, migrated with Terah his father,
and Nahor his brother,
and Lot the son of Haran, his brother who was burned,
to Haran,
and he hid in it for fourteen years.
And again he departed from his father from Haran,
and came to the land of Canaan.
And in his seventy-first year
the battle of Chedorlaomer took place.
And when he was eighty-five years old,
that is, in the first year of the Promise, he went down to Egypt,
and begot Ishmael by Hagar.
Ishmael lived one hundred and thirty-seven years.
And the fortieth year of the Promise,
reckoned from Adam,
is the year three thousand and three hundred.
And at that time Semiramis, the wife of Ninus, reigned over the Assyrians for 46 years
And she built mounds on account of the flood.
And there arose as the tenth king of Egypt, Pharandis the Theban, for forty-three years.
And after him arose in Egypt as the eleventh king, Pharaoh Panos.
This one took Sarah his wife away from Abraham,
and afterwards returned her to him with gold and silver and cattle,
and sent him away from Egypt.
And afterwards there reigned over Egypt as the twelfth king,
Pharaoh Isokos,
for twenty-one years.
And after him, the thirteenth king,
Pharaoh Sosonos,
for forty-four years.
And after him, the fourteenth king,
Pharaoh Tarkos (or Trakos),
for 44 years.
And after Semiramis, there reigned over the Assyrians as the fourth king, Zameros (Zameis), for 38 years
And in his days arose the first king of the Cretans,
Cres,
the one who built Crete.
After Abraham, Isaac his son {OCR?}:
at the age of sixty years he begot Jacob.
All his life was one hundred and eighty years.
